mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.2% triggers a preemptive S&P 500 forward return discount as investors anticipate rate hikes, leading to negative 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.2% in a given month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during inflation spikes (p > 0.05), or CPIAUCSL does not exceed 0.2% threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in PAYEMS employment exceeds 10,000 jobs, indicating labor market strengthening, which precedes a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as confidence rises.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or flat despite PAYEMS exceeding 10,000 for ≥2 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in HOUST industrial production of ≥2% signals weakening demand, which predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as investors anticipate economic softening.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines ≥2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive when demand indicators show such declines.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in INDPRO (≥5% in a month) reflects supply-side weakness, which is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates lower corporate profits.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive during INDPRO declines of this magnitude.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in FEDFUNDS rates below 4% creates a risk-on environment, producing a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as discount rates fall.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS declines for 3 consecutive months below 4%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than baseline during such rate declines.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in UNRATE and PAYEMS above 4.5% and 10,000, respectively, signal tight labor markets and higher wage expectations, driving a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 4.5% AND PAYEMS > 10,000 in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when both triggers are met.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month decline in GDPC1 personal consumption (≥3% per month) indicates weakening demand, which predicts a negative S&P 5-day forward return as short-term investors react to softening spending.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines ≥3% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive despite the identified demand decline.

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to supply-side easing when RSAFS (raw materials orders) rises by >8% in a month coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as producers signal capacity expansion.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by >8% in a month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive during such supply strength.
